1.21.1.0.560.0:
### 0.560.0

**Shorter portal carriages, and a seamless crossing**

Portal corridors now come in two lengths. Alongside the long corridor that stretches into the carriage behind it, there is a new one exactly the size of an ordinary carriage — and each portal on the train picks between them, so they no longer all feel the same. Crossing one is smoother too: the door ahead of you is always a real one, changing your mind partway along works, and standing in a doorway never moves you.

- A new carriage-length portal corridor, with its own interior and ten furnishing variants
- Roughly half of the portals you meet are the new shorter kind
- Change your mind partway along a portal corridor and walk straight back out onto the train
- The door in front of you is always one that opens — no more walking into a dead one
- Standing in a portal doorway no longer moves you
1.21.1.0.559.0:
### 0.559.0

**Ride photos for building in a drifting carriage, and for arriving in a Train Dimension**

The camera that quietly takes photos of your run now watches for two more moments. Leave your marks on a drifting carriage — somebody else's build that has come to your train — and it takes a photo of the work. Walk a hallway portal and stay a while in the room on the other side, and it takes a wide shot of wherever you have ended up. Both turn up in your gallery and on the death screen with the rest of the run. The Train Dimension photo waits until you have actually walked in and looked around, so it shows the room rather than the doorway, and it is framed to stay inside the room you are standing in rather than the identical one next door.

- New photo taken when you build in a drifting carriage
- New photo taken once you have arrived inside a Train Dimension
- Train Dimension photos are framed from inside the room you are in, never from the copy next door or from inside a corridor
1.21.1.0.558.0:
### 0.558.0

**Armor stands you place on a train now stay with the train**

Placing an armor stand inside a carriage used to look like nothing happened — the stand really was created, but it ended up in the carriage's internal building space rather than on the train you were standing on, where nobody could ever see it. Placed stands now ride the carriage they were put on, staying put as the train moves and surviving a reload.

- Armor stands can be placed and displayed inside carriages
- Placed stands stay locked to their carriage while the train moves
- They survive carriage unloading and world reload
1.21.1.0.557.0:
### 0.557.0

**Help Translate on the Ways to Help page**

If you play Dungeon Train in a language that was machine-translated, the Ways to Help page now offers you the translation editor directly - so fixing the lines that read wrong sits alongside donating, sharing and feedback as a way to help. The page also scrolls now, and its Done button stays put at the bottom instead of sliding off the edge of a small window.

- New "Help Translate" section on the Ways to Help page, shown when your language still has AI-translated lines nobody has reviewed
- The Ways to Help page scrolls, and Done is pinned to the bottom so it can never be pushed off-screen

**Video Tools page for content creators**

A new Video Tools button on the title menu, for anyone filming Dungeon Train. Each of the two filming commands gets a tile playing a clip of what it actually looks like — cinematographer mode, which flies you through the train in spectator with every door swinging open ahead of you, and the intro cinematic, which you can replay from anywhere in a run. Click a tile for the full rundown. The page also points you at #streams-and-media-of-dungeontrain to share what you make, and at the dev if you need a hand with a shot.

- New Video Tools page on the title menu, with an animated tile per filming command
- /dt cinematographer — spectator flight with auto-opening doors (including on the moving train), an adjustable door radius, and clear-view for shots through walls
- /dt cinematic — replay the intro cinematic from anywhere, or press C in spectator
- Flags that cinematographer mode puts the run into Free Play, while replaying the cinematic does not
- Discord moves to a logomark button above Credits, freeing its old slot for Video Tools
1.21.1.0.556.0:
### 0.556.0

**Train Dimensions — doors on the train that open somewhere else**

Somewhere past your first stretch of track, a corridor between two carriages stops being a corridor. Walk it and the sound of the train falls away behind you, and you come out in a room that could never have fitted inside the carriage you stepped into — a hall, a library, a place of beams and sculk, some of them going on for as long as you care to keep walking. What you find is drawn from how far you have come, so late portals open onto places the early ones never do, and every portal rolls its own room: chests you loot stay looted when you walk back in. The train keeps rolling while you look around, and the ground you cover in there counts toward your journey. Nothing strands you — there is always a way back out — and if you would rather the door weren't there at all, breaking through the corridor's outer wall closes that portal for good.

**Editor: middle-click copies a cell's block variants**

In the block-variant editor, middle-clicking a cell that has variants now puts that cell's whole variant list in your hand as a clipboard item — no opening the Z menu, no hunting through your backpack for it. If the same clipboard is already on your hotbar it just switches to that slot, and middle-clicking anything else still does a normal pick-block.

- Middle-click a variant cell to copy it straight to your hotbar
- Switches to the matching clipboard when you already have one
- Vanilla pick-block still works on every other block

**Resizing a portal room now grows it from both ends**

In the room editor, the length and width steppers alternate which wall moves, so a room grows outwards from what you have built instead of always off the far end. Shrinking is no longer one-way: the row you crop is remembered for this world, and stepping the size back up puts those blocks, their variants and their chest contents back exactly as they were. Resizing also keeps whatever you have built since your last save, and Reset now puts a room's dimensions back along with its blocks.

- Length and width grow and shrink from alternating ends; height still moves only its ceiling
- A row removed by shrinking comes back if you grow the room again
- Resizing no longer discards edits made since your last save
- Reset restores the saved size, not just the saved blocks

**Villagers price up the item you are holding**

Updated the bundled Trade Everything mod. A villager's Trade Anything slot now cycles through what it will take and previews the price for the item you are currently holding, so you can see what a trade is worth before you make it.

- Held-item price preview in the Trade Anything slot
- Cycling Trade Anything icon

**More variety in one of the small path rooms**

A pass over the pathssmall portal room: more of its blocks now vary between copies, and more of its containers roll from curated pools, so repeat visits look and loot differently.

### 0.555.0

**Difficulty set by command no longer follows you into a new world or a new life**

Setting the difficulty by command — /dungeontrain difficulty, or the difficulty /dtp applies when it drops you somewhere far down the line — used to be written once and left everywhere: start a brand-new world and it opened at whatever tier you last set, and dying didn't undo it either, so a fresh run carried on at a difficulty it never earned. That setting now belongs to the world you set it in. A new world starts on automatic, dying puts you back on automatic, and the world you set it in still remembers it when you come back.

- A newly created world no longer inherits a difficulty set in another world
- Dying resets the difficulty back to automatic — the new run scales from real travel again
- Reloading the world you set it in keeps the difficulty you set
- On a server with other players still riding, one player's death leaves the difficulty alone

### 0.554.0

**Each difficulty is now its own run**

Peaceful, Easy, Normal and Hard each keep their own gear, XP, Ender Chest and echoes. Switch difficulty and you switch profiles — what you were carrying is waiting for you when you switch back, and nothing you farmed on an easier setting comes with you.

- Your Ender Chest is now per-difficulty, and so is the inventory and XP carried between runs when keepInventory is on.
- An Ender Chest that isn't your default one says so in its title — "Ender Chest (Hard)", "(Adventure · Hard)" or "(Free Play)" — so an empty chest never looks like lost items.
- Echoes only return on the difficulty they died on, so a Hard run never meets a Peaceful ghost.
- Changing difficulty in-game tells you in chat which profile you moved to and where your gear is waiting.
- Normal keeps everything you already have — existing Ender Chests and past lives all belong to Normal, so nothing goes missing.

**The rooms beyond the corridors count toward your journey, and two new advancements**

Step through a carriage corridor into one of the rooms that could never fit inside it and the train keeps rolling without you — but until now, everything you travelled while you were in there counted for nothing. It counts now: you cover as much ground as the train does while you look around. Two new advancements come with it, one for going inside at all, and one for finding your way out somewhere far from where you came in.

- Time and distance now keep counting while you are inside one of the impossible rooms
- New advancement: 'Train inside a train?' for stepping out of a corridor into a room that could never have fitted in the carriage
- New advancement: 'A new way out' for leaving one of those rooms by a corridor at least 50 blocks from the one you entered through

**A broken portal can be walked through, and portals stop failing silently**

Breaking open a portal corridor's shell still closes the portal for good, but the pair no longer leaves three carriages of dead end behind it: the blocks between its two doors are removed, so you can walk straight through the group and carry on down the train. Separately, a portal you lingered in could quietly stop working — its destination was left behind as the train rolled on, and walking past the midpoint then did nothing at all. It now keeps up with you.

- A severed portal opens into a walk-through instead of a dead end
- Portals no longer stop working if you linger in the corridor before crossing

### 0.553.0

**The death screen recap now works in multiplayer**

Dying on a server used to give you Minecraft's plain death screen. Now you get the same end-of-run recap singleplayer gets — your fall, your deeds, your cargo, your ride photos and the rest — with Respawn in place of the board-a-new-train button, since a server world isn't yours to restart.

- The narrative death screen now appears on LAN and dedicated servers
- Respawn replaces Board anew there, and the delete-world toggle is hidden

### 0.552.0

**Portal rooms stop breaking their own furnishings**

Furnishing a portal room knocked loose whatever was resting on the floor it was decorating. The single-pillar room showed it worst: the ring of pressure plates around the pillar was broken off and left lying on the floor as items, every time, alongside a fresh set of plates. Rooms are now furnished without disturbing anything standing on them.

- Portal rooms no longer scatter broken pieces of their own furnishings across the floor
- Furnishing a room takes half the block updates it used to

**More ways out of an endless portal room**

The rooms behind a portal that repeat forever used to have exactly one way back to the train, however far you wandered. They can now scatter extra corridors through themselves, so there is usually another way out somewhere near you. Walk back in through one and you return to where you left, rather than to the start. Some rooms hide the way onward as well: the door directly opposite the one you arrived by may be nothing but more room, and the real one is somewhere else in the maze. Corridor doorways are also built from the room's own walls now, instead of the slab of polished blackstone they used to bring with them.

- Endless portal rooms scatter extra ways back to the train
- Walking back in returns you to the corridor you came out of, not to the start
- Some rooms stand their way onward somewhere other than directly opposite
- Corridor doorways are built from the room's own walls, not polished blackstone
- Portal rooms no longer spill the contents of their bookshelves and chests onto the floor

**Portal room furnishings are curated, and their mobs scale with difficulty**

Furnished portal rooms now draw from a curated set of furnishings instead of anything the train could offer, so a window room reads as a window room. The default portal room's mobs now scale with the run: low difficulties meet zombies, while witches, vindicators and pillagers only start appearing as the difficulty climbs. Furnishings built for portal rooms no longer turn up in ordinary train carriages.

- Portal room mobs scale with difficulty - zombies early, witches and vindicators later
- Furnished portal rooms draw from a curated set of furnishings
- Portal-only furnishings no longer appear in ordinary carriages
- Window portal rooms now use the bedrock-lock layout

**Portal doorways stay with their carriage instead of being left behind**

A portal's doorway belongs to the carriage carrying it. If that carriage was set aside while the train rolled on, the doorway could be left behind hanging where the train used to be — and riding an ordinary carriage through that spot would pull you in and drop you into the empty space beneath the world, without you ever having walked into a portal. A doorway now travels with its carriage or stops existing entirely, and a portal that has nowhere solid on the other side quietly does nothing instead of dropping you.

- Riding an ordinary carriage can no longer pull you through a portal you never walked into
- A portal with nowhere solid to land now does nothing rather than dropping you below the world

**Portals stay out of your opening carriages**

Hallway portals no longer turn up in the first stretch of the train. Nothing before difficulty level 2 — around sixty carriages in — holds a portal, so you get to know the train before something that plainly isn't part of it opens up in the middle of it. Past that point portals arrive on their usual sporadic cadence, counted from where they start rather than from the station, so the first one doesn't keep you waiting twice.

- Portals no longer generate before difficulty level 2 (~60 carriages in)
- The first portal past that point arrives on the normal cadence, not after a second wait

### 0.539.0

**Breaking into a portal corridor closes it for good**

Dig through the outer wall of a portal corridor past the halfway point and the portal breaks — glass shatters, a beacon dies away, and that portal never takes you through again. You can always still walk back out of a portal room, so a broken portal can strand nothing and nobody.

- Breaking a portal corridor's outer wall past the halfway point permanently closes it
- Both ends of a portal close together — one hole shuts the whole thing
- The way back out always works, so you can never be trapped in a portal room
- Digging inside a portal room, or before the halfway point, is safe

**Portal transitions no longer flash**

Stepping through a portal corridor used to flash the world for a moment on the other side — sometimes a wash of pale sky, sometimes the skybox showing through where the room should be. The arrival is now drawn properly, so walking a portal looks like walking through a doorway.

- No flash on arriving in a portal room, in either direction
- Endless portal rooms no longer white out as their fog comes in

**Portal rooms can hold enemies, and no two corridors are alike**

Step through a portal and the corridor you walk isn't always the same one — each portal furnishes its own. The pocket room beyond can be home to something, too: rooms are authored with the creatures that live in them, and an endless room keeps them coming as it unfolds around you.

- Portal rooms can be home to creatures, placed by whoever built the room
- Each portal's corridors are furnished from their own set, so no two portals read the same

**The void around a bedrockless portal room closes in as you walk out**

Some portal rooms are built standing in empty space rather than sealed in rock. Walking off one of those and out into the emptiness used to look exactly like standing still in it — the same haze at every distance. The fog now thickens the further out you get, until the room you left has vanished and the dark has no edge you can find.

- Fog closes in progressively as you walk away from a bedrockless portal room
- Walk far enough and the room behind you disappears entirely
- Fixed: the fog used to cut out the moment you stepped off the structure, instead of thickening

**Portal rooms no longer fill up with broken blocks and doubled-up mobs**

A portal's room was being torn down and rebuilt over and over as the train rolled, instead of being built once. Every rebuild left the room a little more cluttered: pressure plates popped off their supports and their drops stayed floating where they broke, and the room's own mobs were carried over and then spawned again beside themselves. A room is now laid down once, and stays as it was built.

- Fixed: floating dropped items piling up in portal rooms, where blocks had been broken by a rebuild
- Fixed: a portal room's mobs appearing twice over, growing every time the train travelled
- Portal rooms are built once instead of being repeatedly re-laid as the train moves

**The music fades out as you walk into a portal**

Head down a portal corridor and the soundtrack sinks away with every step, gone by the time you reach the door. Portal rooms are silent — nothing plays in there, however long you stay. Walk back out onto the train and the music doesn't come blaring back mid-song either; the quiet holds for a while, then a fresh track starts on its own.

- Music fades out over the last stretch of a portal corridor
- Portal rooms are completely silent
- No jarring mid-track resume when you come back to the train

**Walking through a portal no longer counts as leaving the train**

Stepping through a hallway portal used to look, to the game, exactly like jumping off the side of the train — so a walk to a portal room and back handed out Off the Rails and Back on Board for using a door. Those awards, and the one for shoving a passenger off the train, now ignore everything that happens beneath the world's bedrock, which is where portal rooms are built. Leaving the train the honest way still earns them, and shoving an echo into the void still earns Into the Void.

- Portal trips no longer award Off the Rails or Back on Board
- Leading a punched passenger through a portal no longer counts as shoving them off the train
- Genuinely leaving the train, and voiding an echo, still earn their advancements

**The endless portal rooms now carry on past their tunnels**

In an endless portal room, the tunnels back to the train stand inside the room rather than at its edge — but the ground gave out around them. Walk round the side of one and the floor simply stopped: open void, with the tunnel hanging in it. The room now continues past its tunnels, laying its own floor, ceiling and walls right up to them, so a tunnel reads as something standing in the hall that you can walk around. Open-walled endless rooms carry their floor and ceiling through in the same way.

- Fixed: void where the floor should be, in the aisles either side of a portal room's tunnels
- An endless room's own walls and ceiling now continue around its tunnels
- The way back to the train is still a wall with a door in it, unchanged

**Monsters no longer spawn in the empty dark below the world**

Portal rooms are built in an empty basement beneath the world's bedrock, and the game still treated that space as somewhere ordinary monsters could turn up — on a room's roof, in the gap just outside its walls, or anywhere else down there the dark reached. Nothing arrives on its own below the bedrock now. The mobs a portal room is built with are unaffected, and so is anything you bring down there yourself.

- Fixed: skeletons and zombies gathering around portal rooms, below the world's bedrock
- Nothing spawns of its own accord beneath the bedrock layer
- A portal room's own mobs, and any you lead in yourself, are untouched

**Nothing generates in the empty space beneath the world**

The space under the world's bedrock is kept clear for portal rooms, but structures anchored at a fixed depth — trial chambers, ancient cities — were resolving into it and building there anyway: sealed beneath the bedrock, impossible to reach, and pointed at by /locate as though you could go and find them. Nothing generates below the bedrock now, and a structure that straddles it keeps only the part that reaches real ground.

- Fixed: trial chambers and ancient cities generating below the world's bedrock, out of reach
- /locate no longer sends you after a structure buried under the bedrock
- The space beneath the bedrock stays clear for portal rooms

**Cave noises carry through the portal rooms**

A portal room is meant to feel a long way from the train: the soundtrack fades out as you walk the tunnel and there is none at all once you are inside. That left the rooms completely silent, which read as nothing there rather than somewhere else. The old familiar cave noises now turn up while you are in a portal room — the same distant groans and drips you get deep underground, drifting in from somewhere past the walls every half-minute to a few minutes. They stop at the room: the tunnels back to the train still carry the engine and the last of the music, and nothing follows you back aboard.

- Cave noises now play while you are inside a portal room
- They come and go on their own, roughly every 30 seconds to 3 minutes
- The tunnels back to the train are unchanged — engine and fading music as before
- Controlled by the Ambient volume slider, like cave noises anywhere else

**Every portal room is its own room**

Portal rooms all looked the same. Two portals that drew the same kind of room were identical down to the block — same walls, same chests, same contents — so the tenth portal you walked was the first one again. Each portal now rolls its own room, from where it sits on the train. Walk back into one you've already been through and it is still the room you left, chests and all.

- Each portal's room rolls its own blocks, chests and furnishings
- Rooms you have already looted stay looted when you walk back in

**Portal rooms are themed to how far you have travelled**

The room behind a portal is no longer drawn from the whole pool every time. Each room — and each of its sub-variants — can now be limited to a stretch of the run, so early portals open onto different places than late ones. Comes with a batch of authored rooms: a new zombie room, furnished starting rooms with loot chests and mobs, and reworked beam and sculk rooms.

- Portal rooms are drawn to match your progress through the run
- New zombie portal room
- The starting portal rooms are furnished with loot chests, mobs and more block variety
- Reworked beam and sculk rooms
1.21.1.0.552.0:
### 0.552.0

**Mod recommendations now come after the support page**

On the death screen, the page asking which of your other mods you'd recommend now appears after the support page, just before you board again. Same pages, new order.

- Mod recommendations moved after 'support the line'

**Fix your language's own text, from inside the game**

Dungeon Train speaks nineteen languages besides English, and most of those lines were written by a machine. If one of them reads wrong to you, you can now fix it yourself: Options → Language → Help Translate opens the mod's whole vocabulary, line by line, with the English original beside each one and your language's current wording ready to edit. Send your fixes in and, once a human has read them, they reach everyone playing in that language — no update to install. Your name goes on them in the credits, unless you would rather it did not.

- Help Translate sits on the language screen, and on the title screen beside the language button
- Every line the mod ships, with filters for what a human has never checked
- Work in a batch and send it when it is ready — nothing leaves the game until you press Submit
- Approved fixes arrive when the game starts or you change language
- A fix applies to the version it was written against and later ones, so an old fix never overwrites newer wording
- Export and import the files if you would rather work outside the game
- Translators are named in the credits, and the language list's AI marker retreats as lines get human-checked
- Submitting needs network consent, like everything else that carries your name
1.21.1.0.551.0:
### 0.551.0

**Discord and Support the Mod are now in the pause menu**

The two links that used to live only on the main menu are now a keypress away mid-run. Press Esc and you'll find Discord and Support the Mod where Minecraft's Feedback and Report Bugs buttons used to sit — bug reports for Dungeon Train go through the mod's own report form on the death screen, so those vanilla links were pointing at the wrong place anyway.

- Discord invite reachable from the in-game Esc menu
- Support the Mod reachable without quitting to the main menu

### 0.550.0

**Your mod recommendations reach the creator**

When you recommend a mod on the death screen — or ask for one that isn't supported yet — the reason you write is now sent along with it, so Brennan can actually read why. Requests keep the name you typed, which is the only name they have.

- The mod you name and the reason you give travel together, instead of the reason living only in a Discord channel
- Asking for a mod that isn't supported now records what you asked for, not just that you asked
1.21.1.0.549.0:
### 0.549.0

**Simplified Chinese: full human translation review**

老本願 has reviewed Dungeon Train's Simplified Chinese translation end to end. 97 interface lines were rewritten and 18 confirmed, taking 简体中文 to 96.5% human-reviewed — the menus, consent screens, advancements and shared-carriage messages now read as written Chinese rather than machine translation. Four in-world books were translated for the first time, so every random book you can find now has a Chinese edition, and two more picked up their newest entries.

- 97 interface lines rewritten by a human translator, 18 confirmed
- Four in-world books translated into Chinese for the first time — full coverage
- New drifting-carriage entries added to Quiet Rules and the Train Glossary
- 简体中文 now shows as human-reviewed in the language list
1.21.1.0.548.0:
### 0.548.0

**Carriages you've walked away from stop running their mobs**

A long train used to keep every mob in every carriage you had already passed thinking at full speed, forever. Now, once every player has been more than 55 blocks from a carriage for a few seconds, that carriage's mobs are set aside — and restored the moment someone comes back, exactly as you left them: villager trades, gear, inventories, names and positions all intact. Half-loot a carriage, wander off, come back, and you'll find what you left rather than a fresh roll. This mostly helps dedicated servers and multiplayer, where mobs on carriages nobody is near were pure overhead. You may occasionally spot mobs in a far-off carriage blink out and reappear as you get closer; that's this at work.

- Mobs on carriages no player is near are stored instead of running AI
- Restored exactly as you left them — villager trades and half-looted state included
- Server operators can toggle it with /dungeontrain debug contentsdespawn on|off|status

**New "Dungeon Train (Flat)" world type**

Creating a world now offers "Dungeon Train (Flat)" alongside the usual Dungeon Train option. The train runs across level ground with no terrain generation at all, which makes it a calm place to build, test contraptions, or just watch the train without the landscape getting in the way. One thing to know before you pick it: because nothing is generated around the track, the shifting terrain bands don't appear either — no disintegration stretch and no Nether transition. Choose the normal Dungeon Train world type if you want those.

- Pick "Dungeon Train (Flat)" from the world type list when creating a world
- Level ground the whole way, with no terrain generation
- Band content (disintegration, Nether transition) does not generate in flat worlds
1.21.1.0.547.0:
### 0.547.0

**Pick an amount: three price points on the support pages**

The Ways to Help page and the death-screen Contribute window now lead with three named amounts instead of asking you to invent one — $10 Help The Dev, $30 A Big Fan, and $70 Server Costs, which covers a whole month of running the servers. Each opens a checkout with your player name already filled in. Giving a custom amount or setting up a monthly pledge on Patreon are both still there, tucked underneath.

- Three named amounts on both support screens: $10, $30 and $70 AUD
- $70 covers a full month of Dungeon Train's server costs
- Custom Amount and Recurring are still available below the three amounts
- Translated into all 19 languages

### 0.546.0

**Editing a weight no longer unlinks a template from its Stage**

In the in-world editor, changing the weight of a carriage, contents, or track-side variant that was linked to a Stage silently detached it — the row quietly stopped following its Stage and froze on whatever stale spawn gate had been snapshotted. Weight and gate edits now keep the Stage link.

- Affects all three weight editors: carriages, carriage contents, and track-side variants.
- Templates already unlinked by this bug cannot be recovered automatically — the link is gone from disk and needs setting again in the editor.
- Editing a spawn gate by command on a Stage-linked template now warns that the inline gate won't take effect until you detach the template to Custom.
1.21.1.0.545.0:
### 0.545.0

**Death screen financial numbers updated**

The support page's figures have been reworked.

### 0.544.0

**Recommend your favourite mods from the death screen**

If you play with mods beyond Dungeon Train and its modpack, the death screen now has a new page asking which of them you'd recommend to the creator. Your mods appear as a grid, ordered by how many other Dungeon Train players run them. Pick one, say why in a line, and send — then pick another, as many as you like. There's also a tile for naming a mod you don't have but wish the train supported. Nothing is sent unless you write something, and the page only ever appears if you're running mods of your own.

- New death-screen page: recommend the mods you play with
- Your mods are ranked by how many other players run them
- Ask for a mod you don't have yet
- Only appears if you run mods outside Dungeon Train and its modpack
1.21.1.0.543.0:
### 0.543.0

**Love Notes — an echo that comes back loving you**

The Death Note has a mirror. Sign a book titled "Love Note" naming another player and it burns away in pink flame instead of soul-fire. When you later die, an echo of you waits for them at the carriage depth you fell at — and greets them instead of hunting them. It hands over what it is carrying, steps in when something attacks them, and never once raises a hand to them. Same book and quill, same price (you still have to die first), opposite intent.

- The echo arrives with the highest possible regard for the one you named: it greets rather than attacks, gives them what it has, and defends them even when badly outmatched.
- Once your Love Note lands, your next lightning strike brings you its story — how they took it, and whether they took it at all.
- A new advancement, Loved Back, for giving something back to the echo that came all that way for you.
- Every language has its own Love Note title, and naming your book that works too.

### 0.542.0

**Resetting the train no longer strands drifting carriages**

Spawning a fresh train used to quietly abandon any drifting carriages riding on the old one: edits you'd made to them were lost along with the deleted train, and the builds stayed locked to your world for up to an hour before anyone else could receive them. They're now handed back properly before the old train is taken apart. The reset command itself also got two fixes — it always places the new train on the track now, instead of wherever you happened to be standing, and it can no longer leave you with no train at all.

- Edits you made to a drifting carriage survive a train reset instead of vanishing with the old train.
- Drifting carriage builds return to the pool straight away, rather than staying locked to your world until they time out.
- The train always spawns on the track, and you're set down on the flatbed once it settles.
- Removed the carriage count from the spawn command — passing zero deleted your train and then refused to build a new one. Set the window with '/dungeontrain carriages' instead.

### 0.541.0

**Where the Writing Goes, in 19 languages**

The found book added last release is now readable in every language the mod supports — all eight accounts, translated.

- Machine-translated (Opus 5) and marked as such in the translation credits, so a human translator can review it later.
1.21.1.0.539.0:
### 0.539.0

**Cursed books — find out what your Death Note did**

Sign a Death Note, die, and your echo goes hunting in a world you will never see. Until now that was the end of it for you. Now, once your curse actually lands, the next lightning strike brings you a black-violet book telling the story of it: who it found, the carriage it waited at, how long it waited, what it was still carrying, how the fight went, and how it ended. One story per curse — read it and it is gone; ignore it and it comes back next life.

- A cursed welcome book, delivered when one of your Death Note curses lands
- The whole encounter, not just the outcome: gear, the beats of the fight, and who walked away
- Three books, one per ending — your echo won, they won, or nobody ever found out
- Delivered at your next spawn, or between carts if the curse lands mid-run
- Death Note echo encounters now post their story to the Discord feed like any other echo
1.21.1.0.538.0:
### 0.538.0

**Drifting carriages only record real changes**

A drifting carriage used to count every door swing and pressure-plate step as an edit, so a carriage nobody had touched could pile up hundreds of recorded changes. Now only changes to the build itself count — placing, breaking, and leaving things behind. Walking through a carriage leaves it exactly as you found it.

- Doors, pressure plates, buttons and levers no longer register as edits to a drifting carriage
- Real building — placing, breaking, gifts left in chests — is recorded as before

**Drifting carriages turn up more often**

Drifting carriages — the ones other players have built and left on the line — were rare enough that a long run could pass without one. They now appear about three times as often.
1.21.1.0.537.0:
### 0.537.0

**Your name is filled in on the China payment page**

Players paying with WeChat Pay no longer have to type their Minecraft name at checkout — it arrives already filled in, so the support is credited to the right person on the leaderboard.

- The name field is prefilled and the page appears in your own language
- You can buy more than one at a time without going through checkout twice
1.21.1.0.536.0:
### 0.536.0

**Three new books ride the train**

Three new books turn up in chests. One is a traveller's field notes on drifting carriages — how to tell one from a carriage the train built, and what it means to find a chest somebody filled on purpose. The other two ask for help keeping the line running: one a reverent tract, one a plain-spoken passenger who is slightly embarrassed to be raising it at all.

- New book: The Drifting Carriages — recognising a drifting carriage, and what to do in someone else's room
- New book: The Second Offering — a tract on the one offering the Creator never asks you for
- New book: The Creator's Burden — a plainer account of what the line costs, and where to find the Support screen
- New glossary entries for drifting carriages and drift-gifts, and two new quiet rules
1.21.1.0.535.0:
### 0.535.0

**Someone aboard has been keeping notes**

There is a passenger who stopped reading books for what they say, and started reading them for how they arrive — which book reaches whose hands, in what tongue, how often. They kept a ledger. Copies of it have started turning up in the carriages.

Whether the train arranged any of it, or the one who built the train, the ledger declines to say.
1.21.1.0.534.0:
### 0.534.0

**A Drift Gift**

The chest-gift advancement introduced in 0.533.0 as "Something For The Next One" is now called "A Drift Gift". Same advancement, same requirement — leave an item in a chest aboard a drifting carriage; only the name changed.

- "Something For The Next One" renamed to "A Drift Gift", in every language
1.21.1.0.533.0:
### 0.533.0

**Drifting carriages: a new name and four advancements**

Shared carriages are now called drifting carriages — carriages that come loose down the line and reattach to someone else's train. Four new advancements track what you do with them: shaping one nobody has touched, rearranging one a stranger built, having your own come back around to you, and leaving an item in a chest for whoever rides it next. Items you leave in a carriage chest now actually travel with it — before this, a gift left in a chest was never uploaded.

- Shared carriages renamed to drifting carriages, in every language
- New advancements: Leaving Marks, Uninvited Renovations, Full Circle, Something For The Next One
- Items left in a drifting carriage's chest now ride along for the next traveller to find
- Cover me in ...leather? is hidden until you earn it
1.21.1.0.532.0:
### 0.532.0

**Shared carriages are actually switched on**

They shipped with their master switch off, so no one ever met one. Now on by default, including on worlds you have already been playing.
1.21.1.0.531.0:
### 0.530.1

**What We Give? What Comes Back?**

#### What can we give to the train?

It has given you much. Carriages, corridors, the dark ahead. What is there to give back?

A room. That is what it asks, and what it takes.

Build one in the right place and it does not stay with you. The train carries it off — onto another line, into a world you will never see. And it brings you what others gave: a space you did not make, left exactly so by someone who was gone before you arrived.

Give enough and it gives back. A room of yours comes round again, still as you left it — mostly. Other hands have been in it since.

Who built this? Who has been here since? The carriage remembers, if you ask it.

#### And to the one who laid the track?

Players in China had no way to answer — WeChat Pay now sits on Ways to Help and the death screen, for clients set to Chinese.

#### Who keeps the kids safe, when no-one else is around?

First launch asks who is playing. Kid mode closes the developer chat and lets through only the player-written books and carriages an AI has judged fit for children. Adult is everything, as before.

#### And what of our Chinese players, who must obey the laws of the land?

Filter out the community books and letters that touch politically sensitive ground.

#### What else?

- Updated translations thanks to 老本願
- End cities in the End
- Effect-less creepers — no lingering potion cloud
- Free Play echoes locked to Free Play
- Trades more balanced
- Dev replies stay in your chat history

### 0.530.0

**The AI badge is showing on Simplified Chinese again**

Simplified Chinese was marked as human-reviewed in the language list — no AI badge, solid logo — because a community translator had been through every line. This release adds about 103 machine-translated lines to it (the settings screen and the first-launch card), which no human has checked yet, so the badge and its blue ring are back until a translator works through them. Nothing about the translation itself got worse; the label just tells the truth about the new lines.

- Simplified Chinese shows the faded AI label again, with the ring at roughly 10% — the share of lines that are machine-translated and unreviewed
- It goes back to a solid logo once those lines have been reviewed

### 0.528.0

**The settings screen and the first-launch card now speak all 19 languages**

Dungeon Train's own settings screen (Options → Dungeon Train…) and the first-launch 'connect to the internet?' card used to be English no matter what language you play in — so the Adult/Kid question, the five things the card asks about, and the settings you'd go back to in order to change them were unreadable unless you read English. Both are now fully translated, along with the ride-photo options, the familiar-book vote counts, the messages you get when boarding a shared carriage, /report_carriage replies, and the Alipay/WeChat support options. These are machine translations (Claude Opus 5), not yet checked by a human translator — the AI ring in the language list shows how much of your language that covers.

- Options → Dungeon Train… is translated end to end: every row and every hover description
- The first-launch internet card — the Adult/Kid choice, all five bullet points and their hover text, and the confirm button
- Also translated: ride-photo settings, familiar-book vote counts, shared-carriage arrival messages, /report_carriage, and the Alipay/WeChat support options
- Machine translation credited as such — Simplified Chinese's human-reviewed lines are untouched, and the new lines are flagged for a translator's review

### 0.527.0

**Adult and Kid modes**

The first-launch screen now asks who is playing. Kid mode turns off chat with the developer and limits player-written books to those an AI has checked as suitable for children — screening for sexual, frightening or cruel content, personal details, and anyone trying to strike up a private conversation. Carriages built by other players are filtered the same way, though a build with no writing in it has nothing to check. You can still write and share your own books and carriages either way. Adult mode is everything, exactly as before, and the setting can be changed anytime in Options.

- Choose Adult or Kid on the first-launch screen, or in Options → Dungeon Train…
- Kid mode: no developer chat, and only kid-safe player-written books and carriages
- Hover any line on the screen to see exactly what it does
- Adult mode is unchanged — existing worlds keep every feature they had

**Political Content Filter for Chinese-language players**

Players on a Chinese-language client are asked once whether to filter out community books and player-written letters that touch on politically sensitive topics. Say yes and they are quietly left out of what you are shown; say no and nothing changes. You can change your answer any time in Options > Dungeon Train.

- Asked once on the title screen, and changeable later from Options > Dungeon Train.
- Applies to community books found in chests and to player-written narrative letters.
- Your answer is yours alone — on a shared world other players are unaffected by it.

### 0.525.0

**Trade Everything: damaged items no longer overpriced**

Updated the bundled Trade Everything sibling mod so damaged items no longer sell for more than pristine ones in a villager's Trade Anything slot.

- Fixed damaged items overpricing in Trade Anything trades

### 0.524.0

**New crafting carriage content variants**

The crafting carriage's loot pool now includes two new variant setups, craft2 and enchant2, discovered via the in-game content editor.

- New craft2 content variant
- New enchant2 content variant

**Play-mode telemetry for the data explorer**

The world-info report the game already sends on join now notes whether that session was multiplayer, so the private data dashboard can show how the player base splits between single-player, multiplayer, and both. No change to how the game plays.

### 0.523.0

**Shared carriages now credit the people who built them**

Step into a carriage that has travelled from another world and it tells you whose hands shaped it — the original builder, and the travellers who changed it along the way.

- A shared carriage names its original builder plus its five most recent contributors when you step aboard.
- On a build of your own that has come back around, it skips your name and tells you who has changed it while it was away.
- Your name only travels with your work if you have granted network consent; without it your builds are shared exactly as before, just uncredited.
- Fixed the carriage entry message printing twice when you jumped inside a carriage.

### 0.522.0

**Developer replies stay in your chat history**

A reply from the developer used to vanish from the title-screen chat panel: the panel treated it as an automated report and hid it, so a message you had read once was gone the next time you looked. It now stays in your conversation where you can find it again.

- Developer replies remain in the title-screen chat backscroll instead of disappearing on the next launch

### 0.521.0

**Your own shared carriages find their way back to you**

Shared carriages you build no longer disappear into the pool for good. Around a third of shared carriage slots now hand you back a room you built yourself — travelled out to other players' worlds and returned, exactly as you last left it — while most slots still show you someone else's work and a few stay blank canvases. A carriage you've already met won't turn up twice in the same world, and builds only ever reappear in the kind of place they were made. Creative and survival keep entirely separate pools, so a room built in Free Play never turns up in a survival run, or the other way round.

- About 30% of shared carriage slots return a build of your own, 65% show another player's, and 5% stay a fresh blank canvas
- Stepping into one of your own builds says so
- No shared carriage repeats within the same world
- Free Play and normal play have separate carriage pools that never mix

### 0.520.0

**End cities on the End band's islands**

The End band's floating islands are no longer empty. End cities generate on them exactly as they do in the real End — the same spacing, the same end_highlands and end_midlands restriction, the same purpur towers, bridges and end ships, with their loot chests, shulkers and elytra intact. Cities always stand on solid island, and one that lands on the track lane gets punched straight through by the train.

- End cities generate on the End band's islands, at real-End density
- End ships, shulkers, end-city loot and elytra come with them
- New disintegrationEndCities config key turns them off

**Shared carriages — community-built rooms that travel between trains**

Some carriages can now be shared spaces. Build in one and your room travels to the Dungeon Train relay, where it can later turn up in another player's train — and theirs in yours, arriving exactly as its author left it, loot and all. A build only ever reappears in the same stage of the run it was made in, so a stone-era room won't surface in the deep dark. This is off by default: a server has to switch it on, and uploading anything also needs your network consent.

- Build in a shared carriage and the room travels to other players' trains
- Community rooms only appear in the stage of the run they were created in
- Stepping into one tells you whether it is untouched or someone has already shaped it
- Report a room you would rather not have seen with /reportcarriage
- Off by default — a server must enable sharedCarriagesEnabled, and uploads need network consent

### 0.519.0

**WeChat Pay for players in China**

Chinese players had no working way to chip in: Patreon is blocked in mainland China, and the direct-donation link needs an overseas card. If your game is set to Chinese, the Ways to Help page and the death-screen Contribute window now offer WeChat Pay instead of Patreon, and the payment page opens in your own language.

- WeChat Pay on the Ways to Help page and the death-screen Contribute window, for clients set to Chinese
- The payment page opens in your language instead of guessing from your browser
- Your name travels with the donation, so contributions can show on the in-game supporter list
- The Patreon shortcut is hidden on those clients rather than leading somewhere unreachable

**Free Play echoes stay in Free Play**

Deaths on a Free Play (creative/cheated) run are now sealed off from normal play. An echo of someone who died in Free Play — and a Death Note curse written in Free Play — will only ever appear to other players who are themselves in Free Play; a legit run only meets echoes and curses from other legit runs. No more sandbox deaths leaking into real games, or vice versa.

- Reincarnated echoes are tagged with the run they came from and only spawn in a matching run.
- Death Note curses match the same way: a curse authored in Free Play only hunts Free Play targets.

**Backers' names ride the train**

People who back the project can have their name woven into the train's own language. Their name turns up on weapons you loot, on travellers you meet, and in what the people aboard say to you — mixed in among the community names already there. Nothing is bought that changes how the game plays; it is a name in a hat, drawn at random like all the others.

- Backer names appear on generated gear, mobs, PlayerMobs and in NPC dialogue
- Backers can also write a short phrase, which shows up in item lore and traveller dialogue
- Every name and phrase is screened before it can appear in anyone's world

### 0.518.0

**Creepers no longer leave a potion cloud when they explode**

Train creepers were picking up the difficulty system's potion buffs, and vanilla turns a creeper's active effects into a lingering potion cloud when it blows up. Creepers now explode cleanly again.

**Simplified Chinese revision pass**

Community translator 老本願 has revised the Simplified Chinese translation, reworking 84 lines across the credits, support, book-voting and death screens for a more natural voice. Every line of Simplified Chinese is now human-translated or human-reviewed — the faded AI marker beside 简体中文 in the language list is gone.

- 84 machine-translated lines rewritten by hand, and the rest checked over
- No unreviewed machine translation left in Simplified Chinese
1.21.1.0.517.0:
### 0.517.0

**Modpack: Jade block tooltips now work on the moving train**

The Dungeon Train modpack now enables Jade (the block/item tooltip HUD) by default and bundles Jade Sable Compat, a small client-only mod that fixes Jade's tooltips on the moving train. Jade used to ship off because its tooltips read the wrong block when you looked at anything riding a Sable carriage; with the compat mod they now resolve the correct block on the train deck, so Jade is on out of the box. (Modpack only — the standalone mod jar is unchanged.)

- Jade enabled by default in the modpack
- Block/item tooltips now read correctly for blocks on the moving train
- Bundled Jade Sable Compat (client-only; auto-skipped on dedicated servers)

### 0.515.0

**Trade Everything updated — craftable-item value cap**

The bundled Trade Everything mod is updated to 0.2.8. Villager 'Trade Anything' payouts for craftable items are now capped at their component worth, so you can't cheese emeralds by crafting cheap high-value items — enchanted and custom-stat gear stay exempt. Also includes refreshed default trade values.

- Craftable items pay out no more than their raw material worth
- Enchanted / custom-stat items remain exempt from the cap

### 0.514.0

**Your own community books tell you their vote tally**

When you come across one of your own player-written books out in the world and pick it up, the train's quiet 'a familiar book…' note can now tell you how it's being received — how many readers gave it a thumbs up, and how many thumbed it down. Only you, the author, ever sees those numbers.

- Hold one of your own community books found in loot: the familiar-book line may now report its 👍/👎 vote tally
- Author-only — vote counts are never shown to anyone else holding the same book
1.21.1.0.513.0:
### 0.513.0

**Support the creator from the death screen**

A new death-screen page, 'the engine room', shows who funds the game and lets you give via a one-off donation or Patreon.

**Fixed a rare spawn hang when starting a new world**

New worlds could occasionally freeze at the loading screen and drop you into the void instead of onto the train, when water or lava sat near the spawn. The spawn now generates safely and always places you on the train.

- No more falling forever at spawn on a fresh world
- Spawns next to water or lava no longer hang the game
1.21.1.0.512.0:
### 0.512.0

**Known cheat mods now switch the world to Free Play**

Dungeon Train's balance and global stats assume a level playing field. Installing a known cheat mod (x-ray, automation/cheat clients, and similar) now runs the world in Free Play for the session — advancements and stats don't count toward your profile while the mod is present, the same way changed Adventure Item Stats settings already do. Removing the mod and restarting restores normal play. The known-mod list also updates online, so newly-flagged mods are recognised without a mod update.

- Worlds with a known cheat mod installed run in Free Play (session-only — remove the mod to restore normal play)
- The join notice names exactly which cheat mod was detected
- Editor and dev commands (editor, save, reset, package, export, import) now switch a normal run to Free Play too

**Loot enchant levels now scale with how far you've travelled**

Naturally-spawned enchanted gear — chest loot, mob equipment and villager trades — is now capped at an enchant level that rises with the carriage difficulty: vanilla levels early on, climbing by one every ten difficulty tiers. This keeps enchant power in line with your progress even when an enchantment cap-remover mod is installed. Without such a mod nothing changes, since loot never rolls above vanilla levels anyway.

- Early-game loot stays at vanilla enchant levels; the ceiling rises the deeper you travel
- Applies to chest loot, mob gear and villager trades alike
- With an enchant cap-remover mod installed, loot no longer jumps to absurd levels early — it tracks your depth

### 0.511.0

**End Crystals stay with the train**

End Crystals placed inside a train carriage used to be left behind the moment the train started moving. They now ride along, locked smoothly to their carriage as it travels — including through curves and Nether transitions.

- End Crystals baked into carriages ride with the train instead of being left at the spawn point
- Smooth, jitter-free: the crystal is drawn from the carriage's own motion, so it stays glued to the deck

### 0.510.0

**Saved ride photos are tagged for the gallery**

When you press Save on a ride photo from the death screen, that photo is now flagged as one you chose to keep, so it stands out in the online photo gallery. Only applies when online features are enabled.

- Death-screen 'Save' now marks that photo as user-saved online
- A new Saved filter surfaces the photos players kept

### 0.509.0

**Modpack now includes Sodium + Iris**

The Dungeon Train modpack now bundles Sodium for a rendering-performance boost and Iris so you can drop in your own shaderpacks. Both are enabled by default; Iris ships with no shaderpack selected, so there's no performance cost until you add one. (Modpack only — the standalone mod jar is unchanged.)

- Sodium 0.8.12 enabled by default for better FPS
- Iris shader loader included — add any shaderpack in the shaderpacks folder to turn on shaders
- Perf-neutral out of the box: no shader cost until you enable a pack

**Dungeon Train settings in the Options menu**

Dungeon Train's client settings are now reachable straight from Minecraft's Options screen (both the main menu and the pause menu) via a new 'Dungeon Train…' button under the FOV slider — no need to know the X-menu keybind. The screen gathers the display-scale controls (on their own Editor Settings page), an Internet Connection on/off switch, the ride-photo chat log, and a new Snapshot Max Resolution setting that caps how large your ride photos are captured (AUTO keeps the automatic 1080p–2160p behaviour). Every option has a hover description.

- New 'Dungeon Train…' button in the Options screen (main menu + pause menu)
- Snapshot Max Resolution setting caps ride-photo capture size (AUTO = automatic)
- Internet Connection toggle to turn all online features on or off
- Hover descriptions on every setting

### 0.507.0

**New Credits page in the main menu**

A book icon in the top-right of the title screen opens a Credits page — the people who made Dungeon Train, and everyone who translated it, shown in your language.

- Meet the team: Brennan Hatton (Designer & Developer) and Wilson Taylor (Narrative Director), with photos and bios
- Translation credits list every human translator, the languages they worked on, and how much of each they contributed
- The whole page, bios included, is translated into all 19 supported languages
- A 'Support the Developer' button links to the Ways-to-Help page

**Sharper ride photos with shaders or Distant Horizons**

When you play with Distant Horizons plus a shader pack (or Fabulous graphics), Dungeon Train now captures your death-screen ride photos at a higher resolution — up to 1440p or 2160p depending on your frame rate — instead of the standard 1080p, so those far-horizon, shader-lit vistas keep their detail. Without that combination nothing changes: photos stay at the usual resolution. Each photo also records which graphics setup it was taken with.

- Ride photos captured at up to 1440p/2160p when using Distant Horizons + shaders or Fabulous graphics
- Resolution adapts to your frame rate so a busy machine isn't pushed harder
- No change for standard setups — photos stay at their usual quality
